items.title: Hundreds of illegally placed election signs taken off the streets in Mississauga
items.summary: City crews are removing more illegally placed election signs so far during this municipal campaign than they have in years past, Mississauga officials say. On Monday alone, the first day of election sign bylaw enforcement, City of Mississauga workers “removed approximately 250 illegally placed election signs from locations throughout the city,” city spokesperson Irene McCutcheon told INSAUGA Canada. Crews have continued that work the past few days, with city officials noting various campaign teams — working on behalf of mayoral, city council and school board candidates — have placed signs in locations that violate Mississauga’s sign bylaw. “Although not confirmed through a review of past data, it appears that the number of illegally placed election signs during the first few days of the election sign period is higher than in past elections,” McCutcheon said. City officials didn’t single out any candidates or election teams in particular, saying “staff have collected non-compliant signs associated with a variety of campaigns. ” Mayor Carolyn Parrish asked senior city staff this week about enforcing the sign bylaw as it relates to candidates’ election signage. She noted a number of signs belonging to the campaign of her predecessor and main rival in the contentious mayoral election, Bonnie Crombie, were illegally placed as of early Sunday morning, the first day signs were allowed.

items.title: Hamilton resident charged in fatal Mississauga hit-and-run
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say officers have made an arrest in a fatal hit-and-run that occurred earlier this week. Const. Tyler Bell-Morena announced the arrest Thursday, two days after the collision occurred. m. Sept. 29 for reports of a collision at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Dundas Street West in Mississauga. A pedestrian, a man in his 60s, was struck by a vehicle and was pronounced dead at the scene. Investigators identified the suspect vehicle as a 1999-2005 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 series pickup truck, and that an interaction took place between the driver and another motorist after the collision, Bell-Morena said. Hamilton resident Aubrey Lawrence, 69, was arrested Wednesday and charged with failing to remain at an accident resulting in death. Bell-Morena said investigators are hoping to speak with the motorist who was involved in the interaction afterwards. “A bystander and other motorists saw the collision, followed the individual, flagged them down to a nearby parking lot where some form of interaction took place. items.title: 69-Year-Old Hamilton Man Charged as Police Seize Vehicle in Fatal Dundas Street Hit-and-Run
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, investigators with the Major Collision Bureau have arrested and charged a man in connection with the fatal hit-and-run that killed a pedestrian at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Dundas Street West. Police say 69-year-old Aubrey Lawrence of Hamilton was taken into custody Wednesday night and charged with failing to remain at the scene of an accident resulting in death. The suspect vehicle, a dark two-toned Chevrolet Silverado 1500 pickup truck from the 1999 to 2005 model years, was located and seized as part of the investigation. During a Thursday morning news conference, Const. Tyler Bell-Morena confirmed the arrest and said investigators are still trying to identify another motorist who interacted with the suspect in the parking lot of a nearby Home Depot shortly after the collision. Police believe that person may have information that could help the case and are urging them to come forward. Peel police say the victim, described only as a man in his 60s, died at the scene after being struck while crossing in the area late Tuesday. Investigators are asking anyone with dashcam footage of the collision or additional information to call the Major Collision Bureau at 905-453-2121, ext. 3710.

items.title: Council recap: September 29, 2026
items.summary: Highlights from Mississauga’s City Council meeting. City Council approved the following at its meeting. Watch the meeting. Council approved a motion to establish a temporary Hyperscale Data Centre Task Force to provide input during the City’s review of policies and regulations related to major digital infrastructure facilities. The motion follows Council’s approval of an Interim Control By-law on September 16, which paused the processing of new and existing applications for major digital infrastructure facilities for up to one year while staff undertake a comprehensive review. The task force will provide a forum for regular updates, public transparency and stakeholder input before any recommendations are brought forward to Council. Council directed staff to explore opportunities to reduce litter and illegal dumping across Mississauga. The motion responds to concerns about the impact of litter on neighbourhoods, parks, commercial areas and other public spaces and seeks to improve cleanliness throughout the city. As part of the review, staff will examine waste receptacle placement, public education initiatives, reporting and enforcement tools, multilingual communications and opportunities to partner with residents, schools, businesses and community organizations. Staff will also consider potential enhancements to existing by-laws and report back with options for Council’s consideration. Council considered a notice of motion directing staff to investigate the feasibility of a seasonal portable washroom pilot program in select high-use parks across Mississauga. The proposed initiative aims to improve access to washroom facilities for residents, families, seniors and visitors while the City evaluates longer-term park washroom needs.
